standard_prerequisites.use: The proof opens by explaining that the tempting duality argument fails because the maps $\mathcal{O}_X \to \Omega^1_{X/k}$ and $\Omega^{d-1}_{X/k} \to \Omega^d_{X/k}$ are not $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear, so functoriality cannot identify the two maps as duals.

standard_prerequisites.use: They reduce to an irreducible $X$ with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$, replacing $k$ by a finite separable extension and using $\Omega_{k'/k} = 0$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Hodge duality in the top degree
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, label lemma-duality-hodge (invoked at proof lines 4612 and 4642)
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives $\dim H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k}) = 1$ and shows that the corresponding group for $X^{(p)}$ is nonzero, which is what makes the surjectivity argument for $\Theta^d$ sufficient.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative Frobenius in characteristic $p$ and the Garel maps attached to it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, label lemma-Garel-map-frobenius-smooth-char-p (invoked at proof line 4616)
standard_prerequisites.use: It provides the properties of $F_{X/k} : X \to X^{(p)}$ and of the maps $\Theta^{d-1}, \Theta^d$ used in the commutative diagram; in particular $\Theta^{d-1} = 0$ and $\Theta^d$ is surjective.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the Frobenius, right exactness in top degree, and the spreading out of a smooth proper family
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, labels coherent-lemma-relative-affine-cohomology (invoked at proof line 4629) and coherent-lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite (invoked at proof line 4662); Cohomology, label cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian (invoked at proof line 4640); Limits, labels limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation, limits-lemma-descend-smooth, limits-lemma-descend-dimension-d and limits-lemma-eventually-proper (invoked at proof lines 4658-4660) and limits-lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre (invoked at proof line 4681); Cohomology of Schemes, label coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (invoked at proof line 4667)
standard_prerequisites.use: They make the horizontal arrows isomorphisms (finiteness of $F$), make $H^d$ right exact (vanishing above $d$), spread $X$ out to a smooth proper family over a finite type $\mathbf{Z}$-algebra, make its cohomology finite free after localization and identify the special fibres by flat base change.

core_obligations: Reduce to an irreducible $X$ with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$: pass to a connected component, replace $k$ by the finite separable extension $k' = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$, and use $\Omega_{k'/k} = 0$ together with the differential triangle (proof lines 4597-4608).

In the case where $k$ has characteristic $p$, consider the relative Frobenius $F_{X/k} : X \to X^{(p)}$ and the commutative diagram involving $\Theta^{d-1}$ and $\Theta^d$; the outer horizontal arrows are isomorphisms because $F_{X/k}$ is finite, $\Theta^{d-1}$ vanishes and $\Theta^d$ is surjective, so the map is determined by a nonzero map into a one-dimensional target, using that $H^d(X^{(p)}, \Omega^d)$ is nonzero by duality (proof lines 4610-4644).

In characteristic $0$, write $k$ as a filtered colimit of finite type $\mathbf{Z}$-subalgebras, spread $X$ out to a smooth proper family $Y \to \Spec(R)$ of relative dimension $d$, and replace $R$ by a localization so that all $M^{i,j} = H^j(Y, \Omega^i_{Y/R})$ are finite free; flat base change identifies $M^{i,j} \otimes_R k$ with the cohomology of $X$ (proof lines 4646-4669).

Finish by reducing modulo primes: for a map of finite free modules over a domain it suffices to find a dense set of primes where the reduction vanishes; since $R$ is of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$, the primes with residue field of positive characteristic form such a dense set (details left to the reader), and there the vanishing is the characteristic $p$ case already proved (proof lines 4669-4686).
proof_roadmap: Why the naive duality argument fails (proof lines 4587-4595).
Characteristic $p$ via the relative Frobenius and the Garel maps (proof lines 4610-4644).
Characteristic $0$ by spreading out and reducing modulo primes (proof lines 4646-4686).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the differential on the top part of the Hodge-to-de Rham page vanishes for a smooth proper equidimensional scheme over a field, which is one of the two degeneration inputs to Poincare duality (statement lines 4576-4584). The proof first reduces to the case where the global functions equal the base field, then splits by characteristic: in characteristic $p$ it uses the relative Frobenius together with the Garel maps, finiteness of the Frobenius and Hodge duality to force the vanishing, while in characteristic $0$ it spreads the situation out to a smooth proper family over a finite type $\mathbf{Z}$-algebra, makes the cohomology finite free by localization, and reduces modulo a dense set of primes to the characteristic $p$ case. The two-case Frobenius and spreading-out argument is the substance, so the claim is H3.
